name: Tranexamic acid
summary: An antifibrinolytic with a second life in pigmentation management, where its role is adjunctive rather than universal.
good: Selected pigmentation or bleeding scenarios with proper risk review.
bad: Patients with major thrombosis risk without specialist oversight.
clinicalPearls: It is best thought of as an adjunctive specialist tool, not a magic depigmenting shortcut.
mechanism: Blocks plasminogen activation, reducing fibrinolysis; pigmentation benefit is thought to relate to downstream melanogenic signaling modulation.
indications: Bleeding disorders in appropriate settings and selected melasma/hyperpigmentation approaches.
interactionNotes: Other prothrombotic factors and hormonal contexts deserve review.

warnings: Thrombotic risk assessment matters, especially when used systemically rather than topically.
